title: login() returns True for every caller; the password is never checked
evidence: app/auth.py:[redacted] The function takes user, password and api_key. It logs, warns when api_key is empty, then returns True. password is never read and no credential store is consulted. The change map shows no other file calls it, so nothing downstream re-checks.
failing_case: login('alice', 'wrong-password', None) returns True (the missing key only logs a warning). Any caller that treats the return value as 'authenticated' admits any user with any password.
remediation: Verify the password against a stored salted hash with a constant-time comparison, return False on mismatch, and make a missing or invalid API key a rejection instead of a log line. Add tests for a wrong password and a missing key.

title: CheckoutErrors alert points to the disk-full runbook
evidence: monitoring/alerts.yml:4-8 (CheckoutErrors, 'Checkout is failing') links docs/runbooks/disk-full.md. That file (docs/runbooks/disk-full.md:1-3) is about disk space and says nothing about checkout. No checkout runbook exists in the payload.
failing_case: Checkout error rate exceeds 1/s, the page fires, the on-call opens the linked runbook and is told to 'check the largest folders'. They lose time on the wrong problem during a revenue-affecting outage.
remediation: Write docs/runbooks/checkout-errors.md (symptoms, dashboards, first checks, rollback, escalation) and link it from this alert.

title: rotate() writes the last 4 characters of a live token to stdout
evidence: app/auth.py:[redacted] print goes to stdout, which the process manager collects into logs. It bypasses the logging config used elsewhere in the file. It also raises IndexError-free output only because token[-4:] never fails on short strings; a token of 4 characters or fewer is printed in full.
failing_case: rotate('abcd') prints the whole token 'abcd' to stdout and so to the log store. Any token of 8 characters or fewer loses at least half its value, and the suffix cuts guessing effort for longer tokens.
remediation: Log that a rotation happened, with a token id or a hash prefix, never any character of the value. Use the logger, not print.

title: web container has no livenessProbe and no resource requests
evidence: deploy/web.yaml:9-14. Only a readinessProbe and limits are set. No livenessProbe, no startupProbe, no requests. With limits and no requests, Kubernetes sets requests equal to limits, which may be intended; no comment says so.
failing_case: The web process deadlocks but the port stays open or the container keeps running. Readiness removes it from the service, but nothing restarts it, so capacity quietly shrinks until someone restarts it by hand.
remediation: Add a livenessProbe on a cheap /healthz path and set requests deliberately (with a comment if they equal the limits).

title: Disk-full runbook is one non-actionable step
evidence: docs/runbooks/disk-full.md has a single line. docs/runbooks/queue-backlog.md:3 is likewise a single line ('1. Scale the workers.'). Neither gives a command, a safe-to-delete list, a verification or an escalation path.
failing_case: DiskFull fires at under 5% free. The on-call is told only to look at folders, with no path, command, what may be removed, or whom to call. Queue backlog: 'Scale the workers' names no command, limit or check that the backlog is draining.
remediation: Give each runbook symptoms, exact commands, what is safe to remove or scale and to what limit, how to confirm recovery, and the escalation contact.

title: Queue-backlog runbook is one unactionable step
evidence: docs/runbooks/queue-backlog.md has a single line. It does not say which deployment, how to scale it, how to confirm the backlog is draining, or what to do if more workers do not help (poison message, downstream outage). docs/runbooks/disk-full.md is equally thin ('Check the largest folders.') with no cleanup step, no safe-to-delete list and no escalation.
failing_case: queue_depth > 1000 fires at 3am. The engineer reads 'Scale the workers' with no command, name or limit. If the cause is a stuck consumer, scaling does nothing and the runbook has no next step.
remediation: Give each runbook the exact commands, the check that confirms recovery, the likely causes and an escalation contact.
